The text below is drawn from , a measure of the priorities of the British electorate.



Below are two texts.

TEXT_F:
Are you thinking what we’re thinking? Britain is a great country heading in the wrong direction. After years of Labour talk, the forgotten majority who work hard, pay their taxes and do the right thing deserve action that rewards responsibility, restores discipline, devolves power, and secures our borders. Conservatives will focus on cleaner hospitals, school discipline, more police, controlled immigration and lower taxes—with clear accountability for delivery.

- Value for money and lower taxes: Save £12bn a year by 2007–08 by cutting waste, quangos and bureaucracy; use £8bn to reduce borrowing (avoiding stealth taxes) and £4bn for tax cuts. Match or exceed Labour on the NHS, schools, transport and aid; spend more on police, defence and pensions. Restore dignity in retirement by linking the basic state pension to earnings and halving council tax bills (up to £500) for many pensioners. Promote saving via Lifetime Savings Accounts and stronger company pensions. Cut red tape with regulatory budgets and sunset reviews; end EU gold-plating; restore the UK opt-out from the Social Chapter; keep Bank of England independence; no Euro.

- Family support, childcare and school discipline: More flexible maternity pay; up to £50/week per under‑5 for working families via tax credits, for formal or informal childcare. Restore order: heads control admissions and expulsions; Turnaround Schools for disruptors; protect teachers and cut paperwork. Money follows the pupil; expand good schools with 600,000 extra places; allow free places at independent schools at state cost; moratorium on closing special schools. Raise standards: tougher, more transparent exams and a slimmer, rigorous curriculum. Back skills and health: 300,000 vocational grants; two hours after‑school sport; ban junk food in schools. Scrap university tuition fees; abolish the admissions regulator; build university endowments.

- Better healthcare and cleaner hospitals: Increase NHS funding and drive it to the front line; abolish targets and Strategic Health Authorities; slim PCTs and quangos. Empower clinicians; bring back Matron with power to close wards for cleaning; invest in infection control and more single rooms. Funding follows the patient; protect community hospitals. Recognise self‑funders with a contribution worth half the NHS cost to cut waiting. End waiting lists this Parliament. Support carers; protect homes through a social‑care partnership; fix NHS dentistry. Health checks for non‑EU migrants; a bold STI public‑health campaign.

- Safer communities: 5,000 extra police each year; slash paperwork; elected police commissioners; zero‑tolerance neighbourhood policing. 20,000 extra prison places; end early release; honesty in sentencing. Expand rehab to 25,000 places; return cannabis to Class B. Robust counter‑terror laws and a Homeland Security Minister.

- Secure borders and controlled immigration: British Border Control Police; 24‑hour port surveillance. Australian‑style points system prioritising needed skills. Take back asylum control, withdraw from the 1951 Convention, process claims offshore, and set an annual, Parliament‑approved limit including a UNHCR refugee quota.

- Accountability and local power: Publish a Timetable for Action; sack failing ministers. Abolish regional assemblies; return powers on planning, housing, transport and fire to councils. Strengthen Parliament; cut MPs by 20%; move to a largely elected Lords. English votes for English laws.

- Communities, transport, environment and housing: Devolve planning; act on illegal traveller camps. Extend Right to Buy to housing‑association tenants and expand shared ownership. End the war on motorists; modernise roads; review speed cameras; longer rail franchises. Protect the Green Belt; prioritise brownfield. Phase out HFCs; lower VED for low‑emission cars; boost recycling; secure energy via renewables and efficiency.

- Rural life and freedoms: Free vote to overturn the hunting ban. Honest food labelling; require the Little Red Tractor in public procurement; reform the CAP; strengthen animal welfare.

- Britain in the world: Spend £2.7bn more on the front line; preserve regiments and warships; keep NATO central. Be honest about war, stay to help rebuild Iraq, and support a two‑state Middle East peace. Reform the EU; referendum to reject the Constitution within six months; no Euro; restore control over fisheries and employment law; support enlargement including Turkey. Meet 0.7% aid by 2013 with more UK control; champion free trade, the rule of law and democracy.

Day One: start recruiting 5,000 police/year; bring back Matron; a first Budget to cut waste and taxes; empower heads to expel; begin 24‑hour port surveillance; set the EU Constitution referendum date.

TEXT_C:
The Green Party’s 2005 manifesto sets out a realistic, values-driven programme for social, economic and environmental justice—putting people and planet before short-term profit, reversing privatisation, tackling inequality, and confronting climate change. It champions democracy, peace and localisation to build shared prosperity and long-term security.

- Economics: Tackle inequality with more progressive income tax bands, higher Corporation Tax for large firms, a progressive inheritance tax on recipients, and abolition of National Insurance in favour of broader income taxation. Pilot a Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates. Replace VAT with revenue‑neutral eco‑taxes that price resource use, waste and pollution. Back small firms, co‑ops and community banks; promote credit unions and local currencies; oppose UK entry to the euro; reform global trade rules. Create green jobs and defend workers’ rights; measure real progress beyond GDP.

- Energy and climate: Adopt Contraction and Convergence, cutting UK CO2 by 20% by 2010 on a path to 85% by 2030. Replace VAT/CCL on energy with a Carbon Tax, protecting low users. Reach 40% renewables by 2020 through major investment in wind, solar, wave and biogas, and shift R&D from nuclear to renewables. Cut demand via a Warmer Homes Act and Smart Energy Councils. Decommission nuclear as stations reach end of life.

- Welfare: Phase in a universal, non‑withdrawable Citizen’s Income to replace most means‑tested benefits; retain and then integrate housing benefit; keep disability/incapacity benefits additional. Establish a universal Citizen’s Pension linked to earnings, replacing Pension Credit. Support families by simplifying child support, raising Child Benefit, reducing working hours, and expanding Sure Start. Boost affordable housing through council building, self‑build co‑ops, LVT, and energy efficiency.

- Health and education: Restore the NHS to universal, comprehensive, publicly provided care; end PFI/PPP and foundation hospitals; oppose GATS in public services. Abolish prescription, eye test and dental charges; expand access to holistic care. Raise health spending to at least 9% of GNP, with a hypothecated NHS tax. In education, fund lifelong learning, expand pre‑school, scrap tuition fees and restore maintenance grants; abolish SATs and move toward Individual Learning Plans.

- Transport: Prioritise walking, cycling and public transport; cut road traffic 10% by 2010; re‑regulate buses; return rail and tube to public ownership; expand rail and light rail. Reflect true costs of motoring via congestion/road pricing, higher fuel duty and freight levies; invest in clean vehicle R&D. Resist airport expansion, ban night flights, and tax aviation fuel/emissions.

- Environment: Commit to Zero Waste with a ban on incineration, a national agency, and 60% recycling by 2010. Levy eco‑taxes on polluting inputs; create an Environmental Protection Commission. Apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation and nanotech; oppose patents on genetic resources; strengthen animal welfare (end live exports, ban battery eggs, curb fur; replace vivisection).

- Food and farming: Pass an Organics Target Bill (30% by 2012); replace CAP/CFP with support for organic, local and biodiversity‑enhancing systems; ban GM food; curb supermarket market power.

- Crime and justice: Prevent crime by strengthening communities—better urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, treating drugs as a health issue; oppose ID cards. Expand accountable community policing. Enact strict gun controls. Embed restorative justice. Tackle hate crime, violence against women, and disability discrimination.

- Democracy: Renew local government with stronger powers, PR for councils and Westminster, referenda and recall; elected House of Lords; a written constitution, disestablishment of the Church, and curbed royal powers. Devolve regionally; enhance Scottish/Welsh powers. Oppose an undemocratic EU constitution while pursuing EU reform.

- Peace and international policy: Pursue an ethical foreign policy; oppose the Iraq war, replace UK troops with UN peacekeepers. Cut defence to the EU average; end arms export subsidies; back an Arms Trade Treaty; decommission nuclear weapons. Raise aid to at least 1% of GNI; cancel debts of the 52 poorest countries; support a Tobin tax. Reform the UN (end permanent Security Council seats) and democratise IMF/World Bank. Replace/transform WTO rules with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade favouring localisation, fairness and environmental limits. Uphold asylum rights: benefits, right to work, independent appeals; ratify migrant and refugee conventions.

Judge whether TEXT_F or TEXT_C better reflects what these voters cared about.

}
